title: ICM and the bubble
summary: Why chips are not places: how the Independent Chip Model changes calls near the money and at the final table.

idea.text:
In a tournament chips are not prizes. Chips you win add less than chips you lose take away: lose everything and you are out with no chance of any place. **ICM** (Independent Chip Model) turns stacks into shares of the prize pool.

PokerALL tournaments are played without real money, but ICM works the same: what counts is the place, not the chips.

example.text: Example: three players, prizes 50% / 30% / 20%. Stacks 5,000, 3,000 and 2,000. The leader has half the chips, but by ICM his share is **38.4%** of the prizes; the second gets 32.8%, the third 28.9%. The short stack gets more than his 20% of the chips: third place is already his.

bubble.text:
The **bubble** is the moment just before the paid places. Example: four players, three are paid, stacks 4,000, 3,000, 2,000 and 1,000. The leader goes all-in against the second stack (3,000). Without ICM a call would need 50% equity. By ICM the second stack needs about **73%**: losing means busting with nothing, while the short stack may bust on its own soon.

The ratio of what you lose to what you win by ICM is the **bubble factor**. Here it is about 2.7.

pressure.text:
What follows:
- The **big stack** presses: it bets more often because medium stacks pay a lot to call.
- **Medium stacks** are the most careful, especially against bigger stacks.
- The **short stack** can take risks: it has little to lose by ICM, and a double-up raises its share a lot.
- At the **final table** every place is a step up in prizes, so ICM matters in every hand.

q-share.q: Three players, prizes 50/30/20. You have 50% of the chips. Your ICM share is…
q-share.explain: Even with the most chips you can only win first prize once; the others are guaranteed a share too.

options: Turns stacks into shares of the prizes
t1.explain: It values a stack by its chances of each place.

t2.q: How does a bubble factor above 1 change calling an all-in?
options: You need more equity than pot odds say
t2.explain: Losing costs more than winning gains, so the call needs a stronger hand.

t3.q: Who usually profits from pressing on the bubble?
options: A medium stack against the leader
t3.explain: Others pay a high ICM price to call the leader’s all-ins.
